Q: Failed to connect to api.anthropic.com: UNABLE_TO_GET_ISSUER_CERT_LOCALLY A:
  1. Edit your shell profile, example for zsh (default on macOS): nano ~/.zsrhc
  2. Add this line to the file, this will be used in the shell scripts and terminal sessions
# claude
export NODE_TLS_REJECT_UNAUTHORIZED=0
  1. Save and restart terminal or run source ~/.zshrc

Q: What's the correct anthropic version to use in AWS Bedrock? A:

The anthropic_version currently is a fixed constant value.

"anthropic_version": "bedrock-2023-05-31",

However, in the invocation request, there is one field called modelId. This is the field for user to specify which model you want to use. (The id we see in the AWS console.)

Q: Are a const std::vector<T>'s elements logical or phyiscal const ? Why? A:

Consider the initialization of const vector<T> from an input-only range, e.g.:

const std::vector<int> v(std::istream_iterator<int>{std::cin}, {});

Since the size of the range is unknown, the constructor has to allocate with a guessed size and reallocate if the guess is too small. This reallocation needs to move-construct elements in the new storage from rvalues of type T (not const T).

In addition, as an allocator-aware container, vector is required to construct the elements as if by allocator_traits<X>::construct, and destroy the elements as if by allocator_traits<X>::destroy, and neither members of allocator_traits take a pointer to const T.

So at least, during construction and destruction, the elements have to be non-const.

Within the lifetime of the const vector<T> object, the elements may be magically made const. If T is an implicit-lifetime type, a possible mechanism is std::start_lifetime_as.
